sentences.text: 2. Sri Kiran Raghu Mamadapure, advocate appearing for Sri Vishwanath V.Badiger, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that on 27.03.2012, when claimant was proceeding on his cycle on left side of Bailhongal road, driver of Car no.KA-22/B-2393 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against cycle causing accident.

Due to same, claimant sustained grievous injuries and despite taking treatment at Government Hospital, Bailhongal and Vijaya Hospital, Belagavi, he did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against owner and insurer of car.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3509 HC-KAR 3.
Claim petition was opposed on all counts.
4. Based on contentions, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence wherein claimant along with Dr.A.B.Patil deposed as PWs1 and PW2 and got marked as Exhibits P1 to P20.
Respondent did not lead oral evidence, but got marked copy of insurance policy as Exhibit R1.

sentences.text:
5. On consideration, Tribunal held accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver, vehicle was insured with respondent - insurer and claimant was entitled for compensation of 6,81,000/- from insurer.
6.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation, claimant was in appeal.
7. It was firstly submitted, claimant was 23 years of age and working as agriculturist earning 10,000/- per month from agriculture.
Despite same, Tribunal considered only 6,000/- as monthly income which was not proper.
It was submitted that claimant sustained comminuted fracture of upper 1/3rd of right tibia and fibula, fracture of left scapula and fracture of pubic bone.
PW2 - Dr.A.B.Patil had assessed disability to extent of NC: 2026:KHC-D:3509 HC-KAR 35% in respect of lower limb and 15% in respect of upper limb.
In Ex.P16 - Disability Certificate.
It was submitted there was also shortening of leg.
8. Under above circumstances, award of compensation towards pain and suffering, towards future loss of income etc., were on lower side and sought enhancement.
9. On the other hand, Smt.Ratnamala G.H., advocate appearing for Sri B.M.Angadi, learned counsel for insurer opposed appeal.

10. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.
11.

From above and since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation, point that would require consideration is:
'Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed?'
12.

Same is answered 'partly in affirmative' for following reasons:
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3509 HC-KAR 13.
Though claimant stated that he was earning 10,000/-, same was not substantiated with sufficient material.
In absence, Tribunal was justified in assessing notional income for year 2012 was 6,500/-.
Therefore, same has to be considered.
Claimant sustained communited fractures of upper 1/3rd of right tibia and fibula, fracture of left scapula and fracture of pubic bone.

PW2 - Dr.A.B.Patil who had treated and examined claimant and issued Ex.P16 - Disability Certificate assessing 35% to lower limb and 15% to upper limb but has not stated about restriction of movements of limb.
In any case, Tribunal has considered 25% as loss of earning capacity which is accepted by insurer and appears adequate.

Thus, future loss of income would be:
6,500 x 25% x 12 x 18 = 3,51,000/-.
14. Tribunal awarded 50,000/- towards pain and suffering.
It is seen that one of fractures sustained by claimant is to structural bone apart from two other fractures.
Therefore, Tribunal Balappa Adiveppa Banavannavar vs Kadayya N.Hiremath on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196914998/

sentences.text: 3 would not justified in awarding only 10,000/- towards medical expenses.
It is found appropriate to enhance it to 60,000/-.

Tribunal has awarded 50,000/- towards loss of NC: 2026:KHC-D:3509 HC-KAR amenities, 2,00,000/- towards medical expenses against bills produced, 25,000/-
towards future medical expenses which cannot be stated to be grossly inadequate and therefore are confirmed.
15. Normally, fractures take about three months to heal.
Tribunal has considered only two months as period of layoff, which would not be justified.
Considering 6,500/- as monthly income and three months as layoff, claimant is granted 19,500/- under said head.

Thus, total compensation would be as follows:
 Loss of future income 3,51,000/-
 Pain and suffering 60,000/-
Medical expenses 2,00,000/-

Towards future medical expenses 25,000/-
 Loss of earning during laid up period 19,500/-
 Loss of amenities 50,000/-

Towards nourishment food, conveyance, 20,000/-
 and other incidental expenses

In view of above, following:
 ORDER  i. Appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3509 HC-KAR
ii. Claimant is entitled enhanced compensation of 7,25,500/- as against 6,81,000/- awarded by Tribunal.
Same shall carry interest at 6% p.a. from date of petition till date of deposit.
iii. Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks.
iv. On deposit, entire amount is ordered to be released to claimant.

Sd/-
